note: Maps every node in the README.md section 2 Mermaid source to the Archify component that represents it. Archify's showcase profile favours roughly twelve primary nodes against the Mermaid source's twenty-one, so some nodes are merged. Every merge is declared here with a reason so scripts/diagram_sync.py can verify it was intended rather than accidental, and so a reviewer can reject any single merge. A null target means the node is carried in a card rather than as a component.

reasons.replayer: The producer and the replayer are one ingestion path, differing only in whether offsets come from the live source or from evalset/replay_offsets.json.
reasons.dlq: The dead letter queue is a topic the consumer writes to on a schema violation, not a separate service. It is carried in the consumer sublabel.
reasons.vec: pgvector runs inside the PostgreSQL container. A3 confirmed that as the deployed topology, and it is why the citation-to-chunk join stays inside a single query. One node is more truthful than two.
reasons.queue: The operator queue is a view of the operator console, which is one service.
reasons.labeled: The labeled event set is an input the judge reads, not a running component.
reasons.redteam: The red-team set is an input the judge reads, not a running component.
reasons.otel: Observability is cross-cutting. Its edges were the longest diagonals in the previous hand-drawn rendering, and it is carried in a card instead.
reasons.cost: The token and cost ledger is a table inside PostgreSQL and a reporting concern, carried in the same card as observability.
reasons.pg: PostgreSQL is the surviving store; the Archify component is named store because it carries both the relational tables and the vector index.

sequence_reasons.V: Same consolidation as the architecture diagram: pgvector is inside PostgreSQL, so the two Mermaid lifelines are one.
sequence_reasons.S: Same consolidation as the architecture diagram.
sequence_reasons.P: The escalation policy is configuration the orchestrator reads, not a participant that receives messages. It appears as a note on the escalate message.
